articles.title: ExoVetter and a TESS Exoplanet Transit Search of Kepler Stars as Ground Truth
articles.abstract: We introduce a Python package called exoVetter that produces vetting metrics and visualizations to evaluate transiting exoplanet signals found in high-cadence time-series photometry. exoVetter is open source, modular, and independent of the mission data so that it can be easily expanded and used as part of different transit search pipelines tuned to different science cases and missions. We demonstrate its use in a pipeline as a way to distinguish real events found in a box-least squares exoplanet transit search of 324,530 light curves from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite mission; we limit our demonstration to stars also observed by the more sensitive Kepler telescope as a way to establish ground truth for the events found in the light curves. Using this ground truth, we provide baseline thresholds for several flux-level vetters and one centroid-offset vetter when using exoVetter metrics on TESS data. Our demonstration also indicates that it is possible to create a planet catalog from the light curves of dim targets (>13.5Tmag) that has a similar fraction of real events to that of the bright targets (<13.5Tmag) for short period events identified in the TESS-Gaia light curves.

articles.title: A comprehensive reanalysis of HD 99458. Not a magnetic Ap star but an oscillating Algol with ongoing mass transfer
articles.abstract: Context. Since 2019, HD 99458 has been known as a unique example of a $δ$ Sct variable with chemical peculiarities of Ap type in an eclipsing binary. Aims. We aim to review the peculiar status of the star with new observational materials. Methods. The current study is the result of meticulous analysis of space-based photometry from Kepler K2 and TESS, multi-site spectroscopic and spectropolarimetric observations, as well as speckle-interferometric data. Asteroseismic modelling of stellar pulsation is an essential part of the research. Results. We find HD 99458 to be an eclipsing Algol-type system with active mass transfer from the cool companion filling its Roche lobe to the pulsating primary. We identified signatures of a disc and accretion with varying rates in spectra and light curves. The system's orbital period increases with the rate $\dot{P}_\mathrm{orb}$ of 5.045 s yr$^{-1}$, indicating potential multiplicity. We failed to detect traces of the primary's magnetic field or excessive abundances, both of which are necessary to classify HD 99458 as an Ap star. We have constrained the fundamental parameters of the pulsating primary and analysed its pulsation using asteroseismology. In space-based photometry, we identified pulsation modes with angular degree $\ell\leq3$. Two-dimensional Fourier analysis of spectroscopic time series reveals pulsations in the form of standing waves with the azimuthal orders $|m|=5\pm1$. Combined analysis of photometry and spectroscopy confirms the status of HD 99458 as a triaxial gravitationally distorted pulsator. Conclusions. Our comprehensive study affirms the new classification for HD 99458.

articles.title: A Framework for Analysing Nebular-Phase JWST Supernova Spectra with Application to Type Ic SN 2024aecx
articles.abstract: We analyse what physical quantities of SN ejecta can be obtained from a single epoch of nebular JWST spectroscopy. We provide an analytical framework, which together with a grid of helium star \texttt{SUMO} spectral synthesis models allows the determination of these quantities for any stripped-envelope SN. Using the framework, we derive critical electron densities for major emission lines, finding values in the range $10^5-10^6$ cm$^{-3}$. This means formation under close to LTE conditions for 200 -- 300 days. We obtain ionisation fractions of Ni and Co, as well as the temperature and filling factor of the Fe/He zone, the $^{56}$Ni and stable nickel masses, the Ni/Fe ratio, and the optical depths $τ_{\mathrm{[Ni\,II]\, 6.636 μm}}$ and $τ_{\mathrm{[Co\,II]\, 10.52 μm}}$. Besides these constraints from iron group elements, one can also obtain the filling factor of the carbon burning (O/Ne/Mg) zone from [Ne II] 12.81 $μ$m, and the masses of Ar II and Cl I. We apply our methodology to a publicly available JWST spectrum of Type Ic SN 2024aecx. We find that this SN produced a chlorine mass of $M_{\mathrm{Cl\, I}} \simeq M_{\mathrm{Cl}} = 5.1^{+2.0}_{-1.6}\times 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$, a factor a few larger than expected from stellar evolution modeling. Furthermore, we find that the SN experienced an unexpectedly small 'Ni-bubble' effect, with $ρ_{\mathrm{FeHe}} = 2.5^{+0.7}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-15}$ g cm$^{-3}$ (or an expansion factor of 1 -- 3 for the Ni-bubble, depending on the adopted model) at 167d for the silicon burning material. We also determine $M_{\mathrm{Ar\, II}} = 4.9^{+2.2}_{-1.5} \times 10^{-4}$ $M_{\odot}$, which from ionisation fractions in our NLTE models yields a best estimate of $M_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 1.1 \pm 0.4 \times 10^{-3}$ $M_{\odot}$.

articles.title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
articles.abstract: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$α$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$α$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.

articles.title: Probing the star-forming environment of GRB across cosmic ages with high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy: From \textit{XMM-Newton}/RGS and \textit{XRISM}/Resolve to \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU
articles.abstract: Optical and infrared GRB absorption spectroscopy provides valuable insight into host-galaxy properties across cosmic time. However, the star-forming region embedding the progenitor, on scales $\lesssim 100~\mathrm{pc}$ is heavily ionized by the GRB emission, making X-ray spectroscopy the sole probe of its physical and chemical conditions. We characterize the GRB-embedding medium as a function of progenitor type and cosmic epoch via high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy. We extend our study to high-redshift GRBs to evaluate how effectively X-ray absorption signatures can distinguish between pristine, Pop~III-, and Pop~II-enriched environments. Using the time-dependent photoionization code \texttt{TEPID}, we self-consistently calculate the ionization structure of the absorber, the energies and the strengths of the resulting absorption lines. We analyze a flux-selected sample of GRBs showing strong evidence for time-dependent photoionization, and search for predicted narrow features in the RGS spectra. We also assess the performance of \textit{XRISM}/Resolve and \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU in detecting these features. In the single archival case with sufficient RGS signal-to-noise ratio (GRB~090618 at $z=0.54$), we find $\approx 3σ$ combined evidence for narrow, highly ionized Fe~L absorption lines. For bright nearby GRBs, \textit{XRISM}/Resolve can detect Fe~K absorption lines even in its current gate-valve-closed configuration ($\sim 3$ expected events/yr). \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU will enable systematic population studies of GRB environments, delivering redshifts with precision comparable to optical/IR spectroscopy, unaffected by dust obscuration and Ly-$α$ forest absorption. Crucially, it will precisely diagnose the density, size, metallicity, and abundance patterns, ultimately revealing whether high-$z$ GRBs originate in pristine, Pop~III-, or Pop~II-enriched media.

articles.title: The Galactic rotation curve from the ALS III catalogue of OB Stars
articles.abstract: The Galactic rotation curve reveals the radial mass distribution of the Milky Way, but its determination depends on the tracer population. Young massive stars are the least dynamically evolved tracer, retaining the kinematics of the gas from which they formed, yet previous determinations from OB stars were confined to the solar neighbourhood. We determine the rotation curve and the solar motion from 14017 spectroscopically confirmed OB stars from the ALS III catalogue, using Gaia DR3 five-dimensional astrometry with revised distances and corrected proper motions. The curve is parameterised as a fourth-degree Chebyshev polynomial in Galactocentric radius and fitted to the proper motions by weighted least squares, solving simultaneously for the solar motion. Uncertainties are derived from 1000 bootstrap resamplings. We obtain a circular velocity at the solar radius (8.178 kpc) of 236.3 +/- 1.1 km/s, solar motion components U = 8.06 +/- 0.41, V = 10.91 +/- 0.86 and W = 7.53 +/- 0.14 km/s, and Oort constants A = 16.35 +/- 0.21 and B = -12.54 +/- 0.19 km/s/kpc. The curve rises inside the solar circle and declines gently beyond it, with a local gradient of -3.81 +/- 0.38 km/s/kpc, and is constrained between 5.5 and 11 kpc. Because the tracer is dynamically cold and the proper motions are fitted directly, no asymmetric drift correction or Jeans modelling is required, so the systematics differ from those affecting older tracers. The gentle decline beyond the solar radius agrees with determinations from older tracers where they overlap, making it unlikely to be a methodological artefact. Only the solar radial motion is poorly constrained by tangential data, without affecting the curve. The stars departing most from the curve (1474 to 1662, depending on the selection criterion) form the largest sample of OB runaway candidates to date, to be analysed in a forthcoming paper based on Gaia DR4.

articles.title: Estimation Of The Mass And The Spin Of The Neutron Star 4U 1728-34 Using Triples Of X-Ray Quasi-Periodic Oscillations
articles.abstract: X-ray quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) were reported for 19 different observations of the atoll source 4U 1728- 34. Three of them reveal triplets of QPOs: a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. Even though they are discernible only after averaging we assume them to be simultaneous. We apply a separate model (formula) for each of the three frequencies of the observed QPOs and compose a system which contains three algebraic equations for the three unknown parameters - the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star, and the radius of the orbit of orgin of the given triplet of QPOs, which allows us to find the numerical values of the later. Error propagation formulas are applied for the obtaining of interval estimates of the parameters of the star. This is done through implicit function differentiation. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs.

articles.title: GRB 260924A: Extreme Energetics, Bright GeV Emission, and Exceptional X-ray and Optical Luminosity
articles.abstract: We present a multiwavelength study of GRB~260924A at $z=3.51\pm0.10$ using \textit{Fermi}, \textit{Swift}, and ground-based optical and near-infrared observations. Its isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy, $E_{γ,\mathrm{iso}}\simeq9.79\times10^{54}$~erg, places it among the most energetic GRBs observed. The prompt emission comprised two bright episodes separated by weaker activity. The X-ray afterglow ranked among the most luminous in our comparison sample at selected post-flare epochs, with a luminosity comparable to that of GRB~221009A at a rest-frame time of 3.5~ks. At a common redshift of $z=1$, the optical afterglow outshone GRB~221009A by approximately 2~mag at 0.3~d and 1~mag near 1~d. LAT emission extended to approximately 1100~s and showed an early excess above the subsequent decay. The highest-energy photon, 43.3~GeV, arrived at 82~s during the first episode; a 14.2~GeV photon arrived at 304~s between episodes. We describe the afterglow light curves through forward-shock synchrotron and synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission, with reverse-shock SSC accounting for the early LAT excess. We connect the early and late afterglow phases by modelling the X-ray rebrightening at several kiloseconds through energy injection from trailing ejecta and evolving shock microphysics. The late afterglow suggests a stratified medium, modelled as $n(R)\propto R^{-1.2}$. Within this interpretation, the magnetic contrast $R_B\equiv(\varepsilon_{B,r}/\varepsilon_{B,f})^{1/2} \simeq2.6$ suggests magnetized ejecta, while the highest-energy LAT photons exceed the predicted synchrotron limit, supporting an SSC contribution.

articles.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
articles.abstract: The origin of the excess of GeV gamma-rays in the Milky Way's galactic center observed by Fermi-LAT has been an open question for nearly two decades. The two leading interpretations of this signal are that it is produced either by annihilating dark matter (DM), or arises from unresolved point sources, such as a novel population of millisecond pulsars. In both scenarios, uncertainties and limitations in the modeling of galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, such as the steady-state approximation of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and assumption of an axisymmetric distribution of CRs, complicate the interpretation of the galactic center excess (GCE). Simulations with full magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and CR transport can provide a new avenue for understanding the astrophysical phenomena that drive galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission. We utilize MHD simulations of Milky Way analogs with time-dependent, spectrally-resolved CR transport to reconstruct diffuse gamma-ray emission. Comparing instantaneous emission to a time-averaged baseline, we find residuals up to several times larger than the Fermi GCE, with a wide range of spectral shapes and spatial morphologies. At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.
